recipes.name: Ultimate Shrimp Scampi
ingredients_raw: 1 pound peeled and deveined medium shrimp
1 large avocado - peeled, pitted and diced

steps.text: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook pasta in boiling water until tender yet firm to the bite, 2 to 3 minutes; drain.

Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion, lemon juice, garlic, parsley, white wine, salt, pepper, and Worcestershire sauce; cook and stir until mixture bubbles. Increase heat to medium-high and stir in shrimp. Cook and stir until shrimp turn pink and opaque, about 5 minutes.
Serve shrimp scampi over pasta. Sprinkle with Asiago cheese and avocado to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Ultimate Shrimp Scampi
raw_recipe.description: This ultimate shrimp scampi recipe features angel hair pasta in an easy garlic, lemon, and white wine sauce topped with Asiago cheese and avocado.

review.reviewBody: I like a "wetter" dish but did not want all that butter. A good trick is to reserve some of the pasta water, after cooking, and add that in to final dish. This works great for a lot of pasta recipes. If the finished product is a little dry the pasta water works wonders wihtout adding more butter, cream, etc.

I browned the butter (not all the way but enough to enhance both flavor and color), added all the seasonings BUT cooked the shrimp separately on a skillet with a dash of cajun seasoning. They come out more flavorful and looking a lot more appetizing. I tossed the sauce with the pasta, reserving some to top the shrimp, chopped avocado and chopped fresh tomatoes that I spooned on top. Then I added a handful of smoked mozzarella and voila!

Yummy!! I followed the the directions but did take some other reviewers suggestions...I added a bit more garlic, onion and wine and not as much lemon. I did not add the avocado, even though we love it, it just didn't seem to go with the dish. I also didn't have asiago, but did have pepperjack and that worked fine and gave it a little kick. I boiled the angel hair pasta and then added it to the scampi a little at a time so it was all nicely coated. YES - you will have more pasta than scampi if you use a 16oz package so just add it all together in portions so you have a nice ratio. I have made this twice and my husband and I just love it! The second time I had thin asparagus and mushrooms in the fridge and I cut and sauteed them and added them to the scampi and that was a really nice addition. This recipe will definately be in the rotation!

I made this recipe for a group of 8 people. I reduced the butter and added a lot of wine to make a really nice sauce. Without the wine the shrimp simply sit in the butter sauce . I was able to make the sauce ahead of time and simply add the shrimp 3-4 min before I served it. The recipe calls for far too much pasta in relation to the sauce. I threw in extra shrimp so everyone would have lots. It was wonderful. I did serve it with the avocado and asiago on the side, which were both a big hit and allowed my guests to add if they so desired. I would make this recipe again

I loved this dish and so did my wife. The asiago cheese has such a distinct, excellent flavor that I loved in this dish. I think it would taste fine with Parmigiano, but those that don't try it with asiago are missing out. I also loved the avocado in the dish, which I thought was a little strange when I first read the recipe, but I'm really glad I added it. I did add an extra clove of garlic and about 1/4 cup of chardonnay rather than 1 tsp. I also added 12oz of baby spinach to the scampi about a minute before it was finished cooking based on another reviewer's recommendation, which I really liked. Excellent recipe!!! I'll certainly be making this again.

Wonderful recipe. I increased the butter by a 1/4 cup, the wine to a tablespoon and most important I used a shallot instead of onion. Since it's like a cross between garlic and an onion I felt it is a bit milder than an onion. I am on a low carb diet so I made cauliflower in a grits texture. I like shrimp and grits so it was PERFECT! I will make it again, thank you.

This was awesome ! I used about 1 1/2 pounds of shrimp and added about 1 Tb of sesame oil and about 1/4 c extra virgin olive oil to be sure I got the pasta dish wet enough. Also, instead of chunks of Asiago, I grated it and tossed it into the pasta I also added a few black olives and toasted pine nuts. Mmmmmmmm ! Will definitely make this again !

El Esposo LOVED it (and he's hard to please!) I made it with pre-cooked shrimp, but based on suggestions marinated them (white wine, spicy balsamic vinegar, spices) for an hour. Use dried parsley rather than fresh (didn't have any), and used the marinade to warm the shrimp--marking it into a thick "sauce". AWMAGAWD. AWESOME!!!

This ultimate shrimp scampi recipe is the best ever! I have made it several times, and it is definitely a crowd pleaser. It is easy to make, however, you do have to peel and devein the shrimp so that’s a little bit of a hassle. I tried using already cooked shrimp but it’s not as tasty. It works better with the fresh version. If you throw the angel hair pasta in the boiling water at the same time you put the shrimp in the garlic butter concoction, the timing will be perfect. (It only takes a few minutes for the spaghetti to cook in the water and a few minutes for the shrimp to cook in the butter so the timing works out perfectly!) Enjoy!

This was delicious. I did add extra garlic and sliced cherry tomatoes because we love garlic and I like colorful dishes. I used Kerrygold butter which is a higher quality butter and I also think it gives it a better flavor. As for the exact measurements of salt, pepper, lemon juice, etc, I rarely measure these things. If you like things less salty or have a family member that salts everything, cut back a bit. If you like lemon, add a bit more or add a little lemon zest. Play with this recipe to make it your own. This has been added to our favorites list and will be made again. And again.
This was perfection! I added a few tablespoons of lemon juice and sprinkled some crush red peppers for heat. My kid was eating shrimp right out of the pan!
My family loves it so much. We did white rice. Amazing flavors. I added few sundrid tomatoes .
I did 1/4 cup of wine and reduced to a tablespoon - added more than just a dash of worcestershire ....... hmmm pretty dang good!!

This recipe is great for shrimp and/or chicken. I served it over white rice. I did need more sauce which I made by adding 1/2 cup chicken broth. It didn't change the flavor at all. So, this is definitely staying on the "home" menu . Thank you.
This is one of our all time favorites! Easy prep abd delicious every time.

Make it 1/4 cup olive oil and 1/4 cup butter. The flavors lovingly belong together in pasta. Also add a little finely chopped celery. I don't know why but it kicks in that needed freshness. This is a great recipe with or without the wine.

I used vermicelli instead of angel hair, red pepper flakes, green onions a must. I don’t put in wine it’s not necessary. I don’t measure because usually I’m making up to 6 lbs of shrimp! This is a keeper and I have made it hundreds of times over the years! Love it
I would add more white wine and a little of the pasta water because it doesn’t have a lot of liquid. But it’s so good.

Followed recipe exactly, made for two people, smells nice, easy recipe. There was a LOT of minced onion that didn't present well with the pasta (it clumped and looked odd). I would recommend shredding the asiago cheese and adding it before you serve to make more of a sauce, rather than the cubes of cheese. The avocado was a fresh touch to this light recipe. As written I wouldn't make this again but with a few tweaks, I think it might be better. - August 2023
